newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia proposes changes to coal mining rules.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia proposes changes to coal mining rules.

text.p: The Indonesian government has proposed significant changes to coal mining regulations, days after similar amendments were proposed for contracts covering minerals, industry sources said on Friday.

A copy of the proposals obtained by Reuters showed the government was seeking increased Indonesian participation in the coal sector by requiring foreign companies to divest 51 percent of their projects to Indonesians by the 10th year of operation.

Foreign companies are also required to hire Indonesians in all posts except those at the level of directors by the sixth year of operation, with the proviso that no post can be filled by an expatriate once it is given to an Indonesian.
The proposals also state that reserves estimates must be made by an independent consultant appointed by the foreign company and approved by the government.
Foreign companies are also required to allocate capital gains made on stock exchanges outside Indonesia to shareholders of the companies in proportion to their equity stakes.
Companies wanting to raise additional capital during the operating period by making a public offering of shares must turn to the stock exchanges in Indonesia.
A senior mining executive said the proposals were handed to miners on Thursday, adding that they had until next Tuesday to respond to the draft.
"These proposals are significantly different from existing rules," he said, adding that the proposed changes were part of the country's first contract of work for coal mining.
"Although it is called the third generation contract of work, it is the first Coal Contract of Work. The previous two were coal cooperation contracts of work," he added.
